To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the controlled breathing peak (0.1 Hz) of heart rate variability is significantly smaller and shifts to lower frequencies as diabetes evolves, and (ii) the new parameters rf (frequency radius) and β (breathing peak power divided by sum of LF and HP) distinguish between control and recently diagnosed DM patients during controlled breathing.
the controlled breathing peak (at 0.1Hz) is reduced in patients with diabetes mellitus type II, compared with healthy subjects.
the breathing modulation of heart rate variability in diabetic patients, recently and long standing, is significantly reduced in comparison to control subjects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the breathing modulations of the heart rate variability in DM patients.
the study of the autonomic nervous function in DM patients, which has important implications for their clinical management and prognosis.
a new approach to quantify heart rate variability in diabetic patients and to detect the effects of the disease in the autonomic nervous regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vagal component of the autonomic nervous activity is impaired by diabetes.
diabetes produces a decrease of the sympathetic activity, a reduction of the baroreflex sensitivity, and a decrease in the vagal activity.
the vagal activity is affected in DM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the new parameters rf, and β are sensitive to DM, whereas LF, HF and the ratio LF/HF are not.
DM produces changes on the breathing modulation in the frequency domain of heart rate variability.
the loss of breathing modulation of the heartbeat in diabetic patients is a consequence of the loss of vagal activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the new parameters rf (frequency radius) and β (controlled breathing peak power divided by the sum LF and HF) are better indicators than the classic parameters of heart rate variability for the assessment of autonomic dysfunction associated with diabetes mellitus type II.
the breathing modulations of heart rate variability are a sensitive index of autonomic nervous system function in diabetes.
the new parameters β and rf are more sensitive to detect autonomic changes in diabetic patients than the traditional parameters LF/HF and HF.
